hook.line: When a friend is in trouble, "you should" can land like a slap. Spanish has a way to advise from a little distance, the way a doctor or a good friend would. Vale uses it when Tomás is about to sign something he has not read.
hook.es: Lo más recomendable es que lo pienses bien.
hook.en: The best thing would be for you to think it over carefully. (to a friend)

examples.es: Lo más recomendable es que consultes a un especialista.
examples.en: The best thing would be for you to see a specialist. (to a friend)

examples.es: Lo único que puedo aconsejarte es que tengas paciencia.
examples.en: The only advice I can give you is to be patient. (to a friend)
You can always tell him the truth. (to a friend)
May I give you some advice? (to a friend)

examples.es: Lo más prudente es que esperes unos días.
examples.en: The wisest thing is for you to wait a few days. (to a friend)
Will you take a piece of advice from me? (to a friend)

rule:
Four gentle ways to advise:

*Lo más recomendable es que* + the "wish" verb: *consultes*, *esperes*.
*Lo único que puedo aconsejarte es que* + the same verb.
*Siempre puedes* + an infinitive: *decirle*, *pedir*.
*¿Me permites darte un consejo?* to ask first.

English says "the best thing would be", and Spanish does too, but the verb after *que* ends in *-es* for *tú* (*-ar* verbs) or *-as* (*-er* and *-ir* verbs): *tengas*, *consultes*. For *we* it is *consultemos*, for *ustedes* *consulten*.

Asking first, with *¿Me permites…?*, makes the advice easier to hear.
smallPrint: Teachers call the verb after *que* the present subjunctive, used here after an opinion.

readAndPick.es: Lo más recomendable es que consultes a un especialista.
options: The best thing would be for you to see a specialist.
The best thing was that I saw a specialist.
The best thing would be for them to see a specialist.

readAndPick.es: Lo más recomendable es que consultemos a un abogado.
options: The best thing would be for you to see a lawyer.
The best thing would be for them to see a lawyer.
The best thing would be for us to see a lawyer.

readAndPick.es: Lo más recomendable es que ustedes consulten a un especialista.
options: The best thing would be for one of you to see a specialist.
The best thing would be for you all to see a specialist.
The best thing would be for us to see a specialist.

readAndPick.es: Lo único que puedo aconsejarte es que tengas paciencia.
options: The only advice I can give you is to be patient.
The only advice you can give me is to be patient.
The only thing I did was be patient.
You always asked for help.
You can always ask for help.
I can always ask you for help.
Did you give me some advice?
Will you give me some advice?
May I give you some advice?

readAndPick.es: Lo más prudente es que esperes unos días.
options: The wisest thing is for you to wait a few days.
The wisest thing is that we wait a few days.
The wisest thing was to wait a few days.

readAndPick.es: Lo único que puedo decirte es que no firmes todavía.
options: The only thing I can tell you is that you haven't signed yet.
The only thing I can tell you is don't sign yet.
The only thing you told me is not to sign yet.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *consultes* or *consultas*. To a friend: Lo más recomendable es que ___ a un especialista. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Lo más recomendable es que consultes a un especialista.
yourTurn.why: After *lo más recomendable es que* the verb takes its "wish" ending: *consultes*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *esperes* or *esperas*. To a friend: Lo más prudente es que ___ unos días. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Lo más prudente es que esperes unos días.
yourTurn.why: Advice about what to do uses the wish ending, so *esperes*, not *esperas*.

yourTurn.prompt: The only advice I can give you is to be patient. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Lo único que puedo aconsejarte es que tengas paciencia.
accept: Lo único que te puedo aconsejar es que tengas paciencia.
yourTurn.why: *Tengas* is *tener* in its *tú* wish form: the ending changes to *-as*.

yourTurn.prompt: You can always ask for help. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Siempre puedes* takes a plain infinitive, no *que* needed.

yourTurn.prompt: May I give you some advice? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Asking first with *¿Me permites…?* cushions the advice.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: The best thing would be for us to see a lawyer.
yourTurn.answer: Lo más recomendable es que consultemos a un abogado.

yourTurn.prompt: The best thing would be for you all to see a specialist.
yourTurn.answer: Lo más recomendable es que ustedes consulten a un especialista.
accept: Lo más recomendable es que consulten a un especialista.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo más recomendable es que consultas a un especialista.
pitfalls.right: Lo más recomendable es que consultes a un especialista.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *lo más recomendable es que* the verb needs its wish ending, *consultes*.

pitfalls.wrong: Lo más recomendable es consultes a un especialista.
pitfalls.right: Lo más recomendable es que consultes a un especialista.
pitfalls.why: English can drop "that", but Spanish needs the *que* here.

pitfalls.wrong: Siempre puedes que decirle la verdad.
pitfalls.why: After *siempre puedes* the verb is a plain infinitive, with no *que*.

personal: Think of a friend who is stressed. Give one gentle piece of advice: *Lo más recomendable es que…* or *Siempre puedes…*
